title: A Tamwick Toast
author: the carters of Tamwick
body:
# To the Wold, with thanks

*On the back of a press label.*

---

To the oaks that shade the road, the roots that hold it up, the Hollow at the end of it and the children who run down to meet us.

We do not ask. We know you do not like to be asked. We say thank you before, so it is said.

*Under it, fresher:* A fortnight full. The cup has a leaf floating in it, an oak leaf, green, in autumn. I do not know if that is the Wold saying no thank you, or the Wold saying drink it yourself, we are busy.

title: A Carter's Complaint
author: Tobin Hurdle, carter of Ashwell
body:
# To the reedfolk at the stone

*Chalked on a waybill.*

---

Six sacks of barley for Nauvissa, left at the stone Tallowday as agreed. Collected. Paid in eels, as agreed. Good eels.

This week: the barley collected, the eels left, and your lantern on the stone blacked in with soot.

*Under it:* I know what the black lantern means. My wife is from Isseva. Whose is it? Nobody on the Westway has drowned. If you know something we do not, tell a man before he takes his cart out on your boards.

title: A Place Laid
author: Bet Hurdle, of the Hare and Hurdle
body:
# Who the place is for

*Written on the back of a table card.*

---

It is not us laying it. We have counted our plates and our pies. The plate is not ours; it has a lark painted on it, and the Vale stopped painting larks on plates before my grandmother.

The card on the front has a name. The name is 'Larkstead'.

*Under it:* That is not a person. That is one of the villages on the Roll. You do not lay a place for a village. Unless the village is walking to the feast.

title: The Scouring Roll
author: the parishes of the Vale
body:
# Scoured

*A line every seven years.*

---

The year of the Charter: scoured, eighty rakes, ale after. The Ash Winter: scoured, grey chalk, forty rakes, no ale.

The last: scoured, a hundred and twelve rakes, the children given the eye to do, which they did very badly and very happily.

*This summer, in a child's letters:* The bowl was empty and I filled it and hid in the hedge. In the night something big lay down next to the stone and drank. It was white. It smelled of rain on chalk. It wagged.

title: The Miller's Count of Bad Luck
author: the Pennyworts
body:
# Bad luck, counted

*On slate, many hands.*

---

One: the milestone broke. Two: the first stone cracked. Three: the Larkbourne moved in the night, a yard to the west, away from the leat.

Four: the wheel turned with no water. It still does.

*Under it:* Five: the milestone mended itself and says no mile. The mill is no distance away. The mill is here. My grandmother says it has always been here, and it is the rest of us who have been a mile off.

title: The Shepherd's Word
author: Hob Rookwell, shepherd
body:
# Tell Rookdown

*Cut on a hazel stick.*

---

The warrener is in the hut. He came up at the Long Table and has not come down.

He will not come out in daylight. He asks for rabbit, raw. He knows my name and my father's and the name of my dog that died.

*Under it:* He does not know his own. When I say it to him, he listens as if it were news from far away.

title: A Sentry's Excuse
author: a Larkbourne Boy
body:
# To Cap'n at the Coombe

*On the back of a tithe receipt.*

---

I rung the bell. I no I am not ment to ring the bell. It is a stolen bell and ringing it tells them where we are.

I rung it because there was somebody on the road with no lantern and no feet that I could see, walking up from Rookdown in the dark, and a boundary with its bell took off it is a boundary nobody is keeping, and I thought somebody ought to.

*Under it:* It stopped at the bell. It went back. Tell them it was the Larkbourne Boys.

title: The Halt Log
author: the Wardens of Hound Watch
body:
# Halted

*A patrol a line.*

---

Four of us, down from the Watch, fire lit, wolves at the edge of the light. Went on at dawn. Arlo, senior.

*The night nobody was out:* Came down to a fire burning and a bell on the pole, a Warden bell, the old pattern with the lark on it that the Rest has not cast since the Quiet Villages years. Nobody there.

*Under it:* The bell's roll-mark is Gosford's. Gosford went quiet in 981. Arlo, senior. I have kept the bell. I do not want to.

title: The Wind-Rag Book
author: the shepherds of Fallowfold
body:
# How the rag lay

*Tallow-black on hide.*

---

South. South. North (flocks in, fleeces washed, ash in the pond). South.

*This week:* North. North, the thistledown on the down going straight up in the still air, and the rag straight out, north, like a hand pointing.

*Under it:* It is not the wind pulling it. It is something south of us breathing out.

title: The Nine Names
author: the Wardens' Roll, as copied
body:
# The garrison of the Tumbled Watch

*Copied fair from the Roll.*

---

Hodge Barrow, captain. Anna Barrow, his sister. Ems Cartwright. Pell Tally. The two Larkstead boys. Oswy. Oswy's dog, which the Roll counts. Old Mother Weir, who cooked.

Say them as you pass. That is all they need.

*Under it, in a patrol's pencil:* Said them. The bell rang on its own at the dog's name.

title: The Cup Count
author: the Wardens' patrols
body:
# Came back

*Cut with a sword-point.*

---

Five out, five back, five cups. Four out, four back. Six out, five back, five cups and the sixth cup turned over, for Dann.

*This month:* Four out, four back, four cups. And a fifth cup, full, warm, every morning, in the place where Dann's used to be turned over.

*Under it:* Dann went south in the spring. We turned his cup over. Somebody keeps turning it back.

title: What Was Said on the Stones
author: stitched by Maisie Wynstead
body:
# Said on the stones

*Worked in thread.*

---

The Larkfields' lark came back. The miller's wheel is turning dry again. The Steward's hat is new and nobody likes it.

*And lower, in red thread:* Mother sat on the middle stone and opened her mouth to tell about the Brow, and closed it. She said she had had a name on the tip of her tongue, a village, and it went.

*Under it:* I will not sit there. I will sit on the end ones and say everybody's names, so that they stay.

title: A Maltster's Turning-Card
author: the last maltster of the Hanger
body:
# Turned

*Pinholes on a card, and the key to them.*

---

Spread: Kindleday dawn. Turned every four hours, three days. Chitted: Tallowday. Kilned: the day after.

My last floor. The mill has the brewers now. I have turned barley on these flags fifty years and there is nothing left to turn.

*Under it, in the same hand, older:* I will lie down on the floor tonight, where it is warm, and see if I sprout.

title: The Old Men's Verse
author: as hummed at Toll View; written down by Ansa Pell
body:
# What they hum

*A student's page.*

---

They do not know the words. They say there never were words. They sit and the bench hums and they hum with it.

I wrote down the tune. It is the Toll's note, and the note under it, and then four notes that go down, and stop, as if something had been set down gently.

*Under it:* The Circle will want this. I do not think I will give it to them. It is the old men's.

title: A Warden's Report
author: Wynn Ashdown of the Wardens' Rest
body:
# The Quiet Mile, a fifth name

*Waxed packet, Roll-ribbon.*

---

Mullbourne, one mile. Harewell, two. Larkstead, a mile and a half. Gosford, three, and the only one with a date.

Below them, cut this week: a fifth name, and no mile beside it.

*Under it:* I will not write the name here. I have checked it against the Roll twice. It is not on the Roll. It is a village that is still on the map. I have been there. I bought bread there on Tallowday. I am going back tomorrow to see if it is still where I left it.

title: A Carter's Warning
author: the carters of Tamwick
body:
# The hollow at dawn

*Scratched on slate.*

---

Trot past before sunrise. Walk after. Never stop at the hollow at dawn to look at the pretty stones.

*Under it:* The polish has gone up this spring, to a man's shoulder. Whatever is rubbing on them now stands up to do it. Trot past at noon as well.

title: The Boys' Gate-Book
author: a Larkbourne Boy
body:
# At the drove gate

*A stolen ledger.*

---

A cart of cheese, four pennies. A tinker, nothing, he had nothing. A Warden, nothing, we opened the gate and said good morning.

*This month:* Turned back: a woman walking to Rookdown with a child. Turned back: two drovers. Turned back: a man who said he was going home to Larkstead.

*Under it:* There is no Larkstead. We turned him back anyway. It is not robbing if you are keeping somebody off the down at night. It is the only honest work we have done all year.

title: A Shepherd's Complaint
author: Tam Pennywort, shepherd
body:
# To my cousin at the mill

*Chalked on a hurdle.*

---

Your wheel hums. It has always hummed. The sheep like it. That was fine.

This week the flock lies in a ring every night with their faces to the mill and will not come down. The dog will not make them.

*Under it:* Whatever you are grinding at night, cousin, stop it, or tell me what it is so I can tell the sheep.

title: The Dew-Well Saying
author: after Hearth-Mother Ansel
body:
# What she said at the well

*Carved on a flint.*

---

One cup a night, and the one who drinks it tells the one who comes after something true about somebody who is not there.

That is how a village stays warm. That is how a name stays said.

*Scratched under it, recently:* Two cups. Two of us. So somebody is coming after who needs twice as much said about them.

title: A Coldharbour Warning
author: the Coldharbour family
body:
# Do not count them

*Scratched deep on slate.*

---

These are the barrow's sheep. You do not count the barrow's sheep. You do not count the stones owed. You do not count.

*Under it:* A Tollmere man stopped last week and counted them aloud for the pleasure of it: nineteen. In the morning eighteen, and a new stone on the barrow, warm. He was very sorry. He is still very sorry. He has been out walking the Brow since, looking for the nineteenth.

title: The Ploughman's Board
author: as painted, and repainted, by Sal Rookwell
body:
# On the board

*Copied from the paint.*

---

OLD RAB, WHO PLOUGHED TO THE EDGE.
HE IS WATCHING THE HUSH. IF IT COMES UP, HE WILL TELL YOU.

*Under it, in Sal's hand:* I repaint it every Naming Day. This year it was turned round, to face us, as if he had seen something and wanted to say it. I have not turned it back. I am waiting for him to finish.

title: The Well-Roll
author: the families of the Brow
body:
# Drawn for a naming

*In a clay tube.*

---

A bucket for Tam Rookwell's girl. A bucket for the Brow End twins, two, which took some doing.

*This month:* A bucket drawn every dawn. Nobody on the Brow has drawn it. Nobody on the Brow has a child to name.

*Under it:* My mother says the well is drawing for the children of the villages the Wardens read out. I told her those villages are gone. She said: then who is being born?

title: A Brow Shepherd's Promise
author: a shepherd of the Brow
body:
# In the ring

*Scratched on a flat stone.*

---

If the ewes come through the winter I will not bring them through the ring. Not once. Not to save time.

*Scratched under it, in the same hand:* They came through. I have kept it.

*Newer, another hand:* He brought them through, the spring he was dying. The lichen is on his door now.

title: The Bandits' Takings
author: the bandits of the Wynstead ditch
body:
# The season

*Chalked on a Warden's notice.*

---

A purse off a Fallowfold carter. A good cloak. A cheese, whole.

*Chalked newer:* The milestone went back to the verge in the night. We carried it back here. It went back again. We are leaving it. It says two miles to Fallowfold. It has always said two miles.
